facility: Great Lakes Water Authority 120-inch PCCP transmission main break (Lake Huron WTP to Imlay City), Michigan, August 13, 2022
source: Great Lakes Water Authority, Incident Report for 120-inch Water Transmission Main Break of August 13, 2022, December 20, 2022 (report to EGLE under Rule R325.12304), with appendices: PICA NFT inspection report and Xylem/Pure Technologies PipeWalker inspection reports (public record)
question: On August 13, 2022 the 120-inch PCCP transmission main from the Lake Huron WTP failed catastrophically about half a mile west of the plant, cutting supply to much of the northern GLWA service area for weeks. Using the incident timeline, operating data, pipe history and the post-break electromagnetic inspections, determine the probable cause of the failure (was operating pressure or a surge involved?), judge whether the rest of the inspected main needs immediate replacement, and recommend what GLWA should change in the design, operation and emergency response of this main to prevent or limit a repeat.

criteria.name: Normal operating / design pressure limit for 120-inch main
criteria.value: up to 200 psi normal operating; 200 psi design - operating pressure did not exceed design immediately leading up to event

criteria.name: Water emergency and EGLE reporting basis
criteria.value: loss of pressure / lack of adequate supply = water emergency requiring discovery, cause, corrective actions, public notice, affected area, duration and coping ability report

criteria.name: Repair disinfection and return-to-service test
criteria.value: fill/chlorinate/flush, chlorine residuals to normal, pressure testing, 3 consecutive days bacteriological samples passing before BWA lift and restoration to service

criteria.name: Post-break electromagnetic condition assessment extent
criteria.value: dewatered main inspected: PICA NFT ~1.58 miles at break (0.5 mi east + 1.0 mi west); Pure PipeWalker 0.62 mi east + 3.77 mi west; visual/sounding for imminent failure; wire-break regions quantified

criteria.name: PCCP distress screening for this study
criteria.source: p.126, p.134, p.169 (PICA + Pure results); no agency threshold stated in available pages
criteria.value: inventory distress: PICA 7 WB regions max 15 WBs, 0 regions >15 WBs; Pure West 27/1248 pipes with broken wraps; use max count, spatial clustering and visual distress to judge immediate replacement need - no >15-WB region found in inspected length

definitions.definition: Prestressed concrete cylinder pipe with steel cylinder, concrete and prestress wire wrapped outside to withstand design pressure; embedded type in this main

Electromagnetic wire-break detection: PICA Near-Field Testing (NFT) and Pure PipeWalker; regions reported as estimated number of broken prestress wire wraps; uncalibrated estimates where no pipe-specific calibration performed
Small-magnitude EM signal with same phase/amplitude traits suspected related to manufacturing vs joint geometry responses (anomalous joints)
Capacity with largest unit of a station out of service - applied to LHWTP / IMC pumping and to transmission redundancy (sole conduit vs looped/emergency-feed capability)
definitions.source: document units rule; p.9 sole conduit statement

criteria.question: Was operating pressure or surge involved in Aug 13 2022 120-inch PCCP failure ~0.5-1 mi west of LHWTP, does rest of inspected main need immediate replacement, and what design/operation/emergency-response changes should prevent/limit repeat?

rfi.issue: Break location stated as both ~0.5 mi and ~1 mi west of LHWTP - which chainage governs remediation and exposure?
rfi.reason: p.11 says one-half mile due west; p.126/p.128 say ~1 mile; affects cover, pressure head and which pipes were removed
rfi.resolution: ASSUMPTION: treat as 0.5-1.0 mi west zone at Metcalf Rd State Rd to North Rd excavation where 3x16-ft segments removed; reason - both describe same field excavation accessed by PICA/Pure, exact station not in available pages

rfi.issue: Construction year stated as 1968 vs early 1970s vs in-service mid-1970s - which defines vintage failure-rate class (1968-71 high-rate cohort)?
rfi.reason: p.126 says constructed 1968; p.7 early 1970s; p.9 mid-1970s service; determines whether pipe falls in >1/10k 1968-71 cohort
rfi.resolution: ASSUMPTION: pipe is 1968-manufacture / early-1970s-installed vintage and therefore within 1968-71 higher-failure cohort; reason - PICA 1968 date plus early-70s install spans that manufacturing window cited p.17

rfi.issue: Repair quantity conflict: 1 Texas piece + 3 additional ordered vs 2 Thompson made vs 3 total replaced
rfi.reason: p.13 orders 1+3; p.18 says 2 made; p.15 says 3 replaced; need firm as-built length for disinfection volume and joint count
rfi.resolution: ASSUMPTION: 3x16-ft (≈48 ft) PCCP replaced with welded joints governs; reason - p.15/p.127 final as-built (three ~16ft segments removed/replaced) supersedes interim procurement notes

rfi.issue: No time-series pressure / transient log values in available pages - only narrative that pressure did not exceed 200 psi and no high fluctuations recorded
rfi.reason: Cannot independently verify surge absence without SCADA trace, Greenwood SN-01 Figure 3 values, or LHWTP discharge logs
rfi.resolution: ASSUMPTION: accept GLWA operational review (p.17) and SCC observation (p.16) at face value for Steps 1-2; reason - only evidence in available pages; flag need for SCADA/transient monitoring as recommendation

rfi.issue: No pipe-specific EM calibration; Pure counts modelled and PICA counts estimated (up to N) - true break counts uncertain
rfi.reason: p.146/p.174 state no calibration, accuracy affected; distress thresholds for immediate replacement not stated
rfi.resolution: ASSUMPTION: treat reported maxima (PICA up to 5/10/15; Pure 27 pipes distressed) as upper-bound screening values with uncertainty band; reason - document explicitly warns refinement needs future calibration tests

rfi.issue: HDR laboratory testing, soil/corrosion, bedding, and failed-pipe metallurgy results withheld / not in available pages
rfi.reason: p.17 study reviewed lab testing but withheld clause hides conclusion; cannot distinguish wire corrosion, hydrogen embrittlement, manufacturing defect, external load
rfi.resolution: ASSUMPTION: infer probable cause from age cohort + rupture at invert + wire-break background + no overpressure; reason - only facts available; recommend exhuming lab report and targeted re-inspection

rfi.issue: Uninspected gaps west Sta 14+84-23+47 and 65+31-68+19 due high water; plus only ~5.3 of 26 miles inspected - remainder condition unknown
rfi.reason: p.172 gaps; p.14-p.15 inspected ~1.58+4.4 mi at break only; 26-mi main mostly unassessed
rfi.resolution: ASSUMPTION: inspected zone is representative of near-break reach only, not whole 26-mi main; reason - inspections centered at failure excavation, gaps logged as water-blocked

rfi.issue: East-leg Pure distress counts and PICA pipe-by-pipe locations not in available pages (only West totals provided)

rfi.resolution: ASSUMPTION: use PICA East+West combined 7 regions as controlling near-field distress for Steps 1-2; reason - only complete tabulated finding in available pages

108-inch butterfly isolation valve at/near LHWTP (closed to restore Burtchville)
120-inch embedded PCCP transmission main ~26 mi LHWTP to IMC (east leg to break + west leg to IMC)
Break excavation/failure site ~0.5-1 mi west of LHWTP (Metcalf Rd State Rd to North Rd; 3x16-ft segments removed/replaced)
Imlay City Booster Pump Station (IMC) with 20-MG reservoir (pumped or bypassed operation)
72-inch transmission main west of IMC (serves Lapeer/Mayfield/Imlay City/Flint via FL-01)
96-inch transmission main south IMC to North Service Center (NSC) (reverse-fed from Northeast WTP during outage)
North Service Center (NSC) valving/pumps + Northeast WTP (NEWTP) supply
Master meters and control valves: Greenwood SN-01, FL-01 (closed Aug 25), Potter-Baxter, Welch Rd access
Emergency interconnections and local sources: Genesee County (GCDC) to 72-inch at Baxter/Potter, Lapeer, Almont, Imlay City emergency connections, groundwater wells
DTE Greenwood Power Generation Facility turnout (unserved during outage)
Appurtenances in inspected reach: 9 manholes (incl. new Manhole #3 at failure + #6 later addition), 4x 12-inch blow-offs (per PICA)
Member-partner distribution systems under BWA (~133k pop Aug 14) + bulk-water trucks/bottled-water distribution

alternatives.cost_basis: Large-diameter parallel transmission, trench/shaft, tie-ins; order-of-magnitude vs 26-mi (p.7) scale
alternatives.option: Build looped/redundant feeder or critical-reach second barrel so loss of one barrel retains firm supply (firm = largest unit out)
alternatives.result: FIRM-LOOP-PAR reports P-EXIST 88039.6 gpm at 2.5 fps + P-LOOP 22971.4 gpm at 1.81 fps sharing 111011 gpm with J-BR 14.04 psi vs CAL-162-FINAL single-barrel 110406 gpm at 3.13 fps; loop carries flow with lower velocity/headloss and single-barrel outage no longer equals zero supply

alternatives.cost_basis: Two 108-120-in line valves + vaults + stocked 16-ft PCCP closure pieces (p.15 3x16-ft replaced, welded inside+out; p.13 Texas priority ship + Thompson order) to avoid 50-day procurement/fill cycle
alternatives.option: Sectionalize main with intermediate isolation valves and stock repair pieces/clamps; recommended near-term
alternatives.result: SEG-ISOL-05MI models 0.5-mi isolated segment concept; full LHWTP-IMC fill is ~81 MG (p.18) and break isolated within 5 hours once LHWTP offline with 108-in valve closed (p.16); sectionalizing limits drain/fill/chlorinate/flush volume and 3-day sampling return (p.18-p.19) vs draining 26-mi (p.7) barrel

alternatives.cost_basis: SCADA upgrades, transient loggers, EM calibration digs, procedures/exercises; no major civil works
alternatives.option: Install continuous pressure-transient monitoring at LHWTP/break/IMC, calibrate EM counts with test pits, and formalize/exercise NSC reverse-feed and emergency interconnections; recommended immediate
alternatives.result: CAL-162-FINAL reports J-BR 13.9 psi equivalent and pipes 110406 gpm at 3.13 fps matching ~162 MGD (p.11) with velocity tool 3.191 fps; EMERG-72-19MGD reports 25301.7 gpm at 1.99 fps exceeding Flint 14 MGD + GCDC 2-5 MGD demand (p.13) and velocity tool 1.04 fps for 19 MGD in 72-in confirms emergency path hydraulically feasible; NSC mode unused >30 years (p.8) needs exercise, FL-01 closed Aug 25 (p.18) needs procedure

calibration.simulated: 110406 gpm (~159 MGD; ASSUMPTION: 1 MGD=694.44 gpm for comparison) at 3.13 fps; J-BR 13.9 psi

calibration.measured: Flint avg 14 MGD + GCDC 2-5 MGD = 17-19 MGD emergency via 72-in (p.13); Lapeer/Imlay/Almont emergency connections Aug 13 (p.13)
calibration.note: Run with 10 ft head shows 72-in capacity exceeds emergency demand; velocity-tool 1.04 fps at 19 MGD in 72-in and 0.276 fps at 14 MGD-equivalent confirm low-velocity feasible operation

findings.evidence: GLWA review: operating pressure did not exceed 200 psi design at any time immediately leading up (p.17); normal up to 200 psi (p.7). CAL-162-FINAL reports 110406 gpm at 3.13 fps vs ~162 MGD at break (p.11) (velocity-tool 3.191 fps for 162 MGD in 120-in) - steady-flow velocity consistency only, not pressure proof. Heads/elevs/lengths/C in CAL-162-FINAL and CAL-162-V2 (138175.5 gpm at 3.92 fps, J-BR 21.27 psi) are ASSUMPTION with reason: no HGL/elev/C/lengths in available pages, heads tuned to reproduce reported flow so calibration is circular. No SCADA trace in pages (ASSUMPTION: accept GLWA review at face value with reason only evidence in pages, flag transient logging).
findings.limiting_value: <200 psi vs 200 psi design (p.7, p.17) per GLWA review, not per model
findings.modification: Retain 200-psi operating limit, add continuous transient loggers at LHWTP/break/IMC and surge re-analysis; do not uprate vintage PCCP without re-rating

findings.evidence: Early-1970s install (p.7), mid-1970s service with 1 prior 1985 break (p.9), PICA 1968 embedded PCCP (p.126); cohort 1968-71 fails just over 1/10k vs 8/100k overall, GLWA 125k lengths (p.17); rupture near invert with inner cylinder ~100 ft away (p.11, p.128); background distress PICA 7 WB regions (p.134) plus Pure West 27/1248 distressed (p.169). HDR lab/soil/metallurgy scope noted (p.17) but results withheld in pages (ASSUMPTION: lab needed to separate corrosion/embrittlement/defect with reason p.17 scope but no data in pages). Vintage spans cohort is ASSUMPTION with reason p.126 vs p.7 dates differ.
findings.limiting_value: 1968-mfr/early-70s-install ~50-yr vintage spanning 1968-71 high-rate cohort (ASSUMPTION, reason above)
findings.modification: Treat as probable age/wire-deterioration rupture; exhume HDR lab, calibrate EM with digs, prioritize Pure >15-wrap pipes and PICA 10-15 WB regions for expose/repair, complete 26-mi (p.7) assessment

findings.evidence: PICA: 7 regions (5x up to 5, 1x up to 10, 1x up to 15), 0 regions >15 (p.134, p.126); 22 anomalies (3 mfg+19 joints), features 9MH+4 blow-offs per prior review (p.126). Pure West: 1221 clean, 27 with broken wraps of 1248 (p.169); Table 2.3: 21x5, 3x10-15, 3x>15 (p.172); range 5-25 wraps (p.174) e.g. pipe 10007 25 wraps at 184+30 (p.175), pipes 10105/12724 20 wraps (p.175-p.176); counts rounded to nearest 5, <5 reported as 5 so 5s may be overestimated (p.174); calibration NOT performed, modelled curve from design properties + other-project knowledge (p.174), refinement needs future calibration (p.146, p.174) (ASSUMPTION: counts upper-bound screening with reason document warns accuracy affected). Conclusion changed: no wholesale replacement on EM alone, but immediate targeted expose/repair of >15-wrap pipes and 10-15 regions plus gaps/remainder inspection. Velocity clarification: 19 MGD in 72-in 1.04 fps, 14 MGD in 72-in 0.766 fps, 14 MGD in 120-in 0.276 fps via velocity tool.

All heads/elevs/lengths/C explicitly labelled ASSUMPTION with reason no HGL/elev/C in pages. CAL-162-FINAL 110406 gpm 3.13 fps and CAL-162-V2 138175.5 gpm 3.92 fps J-BR 21.27 psi quoted as illustrative velocity-consistency checks vs ~162 MGD (p.11) (velocity 3.191 fps), circular by design (head tuned to hit flow). SEG-ISOL-05MI 711423.6 gpm at 20.18 fps (~1024 MGD using 1 MGD=694.44 gpm ASSUMPTION standard conversion) withdrawn: physically implausible (>5-8 fps transmission range; CAL normal ~3.1-3.9 fps) and misapplies pressurized steady-state to dewatering volume.
